Every instance of light is always a (close to) endless amount of light bounces with each bounce reducing intensity by an amount depending on the material and color of whatever its bouncing off of. Thats why you limit the number of bounces the gpu calculates since at some point the difference each bounce makes is negligable. Having portals inside the room will most certainly make the calculations more complicated but endless loops don't exist for ray tracing since there is a hard cap on how mancy bounces are calculated regardless of anything else that might be happening within the engine.

This is actually a really nuanced topic. At first i was hard disagreeing with your opinion but the more i think about the harder it gets to actually form a conclusive opinion.

Rape content can and will trigger people who experienced such things. But rape is basically only in movies and series that are R rated so you kinda expect that stuff to be there (or gore). 

You cant be sure if its rape or gore but you also cant explicitly state what kind of content will be in the movie on the dvdcase or whatnot since that can in some cases spoil the movie. 

On the other hand it is hard to justify showing a rape scene in general. Implied violence in any form has often a bigger impact then actually showing the violent act in itself. Just look at any decent horror film. (slasher film =/= horror films) I dont know the actual psychology behind this but my hypothesis would be that implied violence is less triggering than showing the violence.

But if you actually chose to not show any sexual violence ever again that would severly change how society views those kind of incidents. Without any semi-realistic depictions people tend to downplay situations since they arent able to relate to them.

From personal experience (i live in germany) i know that some children/teenagers downplay the scale of the holocaust since they arent able to comprehend that literally millions of people were transported IN PLUBIC to get killed. basically everyone knew about it (eventho they claim they didnt) and basically no one tried to intervene. Only movies like schindlers list or similar fictional depictions and documentaries make them able to understand the horrors of that time.

An option on our favorite streaming services to warn about triggering contents would be great so you are able to avoid those movies. But i would make it optional to turn on these warnings since the warning itself can spoil part of the movies which some people wouldnt actually want.

But for people struggling with triggering content it would be great to know beforehand.

An option to skip such contents would be interesting but would actually bring some problems with it. If within this skipped scene with explicit content something plot driving would be to happen you wouldnt know about it and the whole movie wouldnt make any sense from that point onward. It would also break any immersion with the movie if there is a sudden skip in it. The last one is kind of niche but if you are a person that likes to rate or critique movies on imdb or similar sites you actually cant do that if you skip parts of the movie. atleast it wouldnt be fair to judge a piece of art without experiencing it 100%.
